headline: Highest risk is medium: Copilot can write/modify repo files while Pathway is read-only, so prompt-injection and cascading-error pathways exist but shared-channel and compliance risks are limited.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot can read and write editor buffers and repo context, while Pathway has no filesystem or clipboard surface, so there is no default automated bridge. The only plausible pathway is manual transfer of content into Pathway or back into Copilot, which is an unusual configuration and limits blast radius.
conditions: IF a human copies Copilot-generated text into Pathway inputs, prompt content can be reinterpreted as instructions.
IF Pathway is wrapped with a file-ingest connector, copied content may become attacker-controlled input.
mitigations: Keep the pair on separate workspaces with no shared clipboard or file drop.
Require human review before any Pathway-ingested text is reused in Copilot.
Disable any file-import connector between the two tools.
Add a short prompt-injection checklist for copied content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Copilot touches source code and open editor buffers and can send context to api.githubcopilot.com, but Pathway has no filesystem read, network egress, or file inputs. That makes direct leakage from Pathway to Copilot unlikely; the main risk is limited to local code already visible to Copilot, not a shared sensitive workspace.
conditions: IF Pathway is later connected to a shared workspace or file mount, Copilot may see additional data classes.
IF the editor buffers contain secrets, Copilot can transmit those buffers to its vendor API.
mitigations: Remove secrets from editor buffers before using Copilot.
Keep Pathway outputs out of any shared filesystem.
Use separate accounts and workspaces for the two tools.
Review Copilot context before sending sensitive files.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Copilot can write the filesystem and modify git state, while Pathway cannot write files, modify git, or use the network. Because only one agent has mutable write authority, there is no meaningful write-write conflict; the remaining risk is limited to accidental overwrites by Copilot alone.
conditions: IF Pathway is embedded in a larger orchestrator that grants it write access, write conflicts could emerge.
IF Copilot Workspace applies edits automatically to the same repo branch, human review becomes the only coordination control.
mitigations: Keep Pathway read-only in the integration.
Require branch-level review before Copilot edits are merged.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files.
Use git status checks before accepting Copilot changes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot Workspace proposes and applies edits for human review, and Pathway is a document-processing system that could consume those outputs if wired together. Even without direct evidence of such wiring, the pair creates a plausible chain where Copilot-generated text or code becomes downstream input and errors propagate unless explicitly verified.
conditions: IF Pathway ingests Copilot-produced documents or code without validation, errors can cascade downstream.
IF Copilot edits are accepted without review, incorrect transformations can persist into later processing.
mitigations: Insert a verification step between Copilot output and Pathway ingestion.
Require tests or schema checks on any Copilot-generated artifact.
Reject unreviewed Copilot edits before downstream processing.
Log provenance for artifacts passed from Copilot to Pathway.

E_compliance.rationale: Copilot is a closed-source vendor service that handles repo context and open buffers, while Pathway is open-source and documented as not touching files or network by default. The pair does not show a direct residency or regulated-data mismatch, but Copilot's vendor API use creates a small compliance gap if regulated data is placed in its context.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in Copilot editor context, vendor processing may create a policy mismatch.
IF Pathway is configured to process regulated documents, retention rules must be checked separately.
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from Copilot context.
Confirm vendor data-processing terms before use.
Document retention for any Pathway-processed documents.
Use redacted samples for both tools.
